pages.text: Expect every fight to cost something. Mobs here are tougher than vanilla on purpose: they are $(italic)real threats$(), so your class, gear and skill investments matter.$(br2)$(thing)Base HP multipliers$() apply to all mobs by category, before any other scaling.

pages.title: HP Multipliers
pages.text: $(bold)Basic mobs$() (zombies, skeletons, spiders, etc.): $(thing)3× HP$()$(br)$(bold)Mid-tier mobs$() (endermen, witches, piglins, etc.): $(thing)1.5× HP$()$(br)$(bold)Bosses$() (Wither, Dragon, mod bosses): $(thing)Unchanged$()$(br2)Basic mobs get the largest multiplier because they are the most common, and they should not die in one hit. Bosses are balanced one by one and need no blanket scaling.

pages.title: Dimension Stacking
pages.text: HP multipliers $(bold)stack with dimension scaling$(): each dimension applies its own multiplier on top of the base toughness tier.$(br2)$(bold)Example:$() a zombie (3× base) in the Nether (4× dimension) has $(thing)12×$() its vanilla HP. The same zombie in the End is tougher still.$(br2)Early-dimension mobs scale up in late-game dimensions too and stay dangerous.

pages.title: What It Means for You
pages.text: You cannot brute-force IridescentCraft with a stone sword. To keep pace, invest in your $(thing)class abilities$(), upgrade your $(thing)gear$() and use $(thing)buffs and enchantments$().$(br2)If a mob feels too tanky, you are probably undergeared for that dimension. Rushing one burns repair costs fast.$(br2)$(bold)Next: $(l:icraft:systems/dimension_mechanics)Dimension Mechanics$(/l), for what each dimension changes.$()
